Cross-asset book imbalance divergence: When BTC and ETH 5m orderbooks show imbalance in the same direction but SOL or XRP imbalance diverges (opposite sign), bet that the divergent alt reverts toward the BTC/ETH consensus within the same 5-minute window. The hypothesis is that informed flow hits correlated majors first and alts lag — a divergent alt imbalance reflects stale or noise liquidity, not genuine contrarian information, so fading the outlier at favorable odds (mid_price away from 0.50) captures a reversion premium.

Spread-asymmetry lead-lag: Compute the ratio of ask-side depth (sum of ask_size_1..5) to bid-side depth across all four assets simultaneously; when three or more assets show synchronized depth skew (e.g., asks thinning relative to bids) but one asset's spread has not yet widened to reflect it, that lagging asset's Up token is underpriced. The mechanism is that market makers pull quotes asset-by-asset and the last book to adjust offers a brief informational edge — enter via limit order on the lagging asset's thick side before spread reprices.

Concurrent resolution conditional entropy: Build a rolling lookup table of joint resolution outcomes (BTC×ETH×SOL×XRP = 16 states) and measure the conditional entropy H(XRP_outcome | BTC_outcome, ETH_outcome, SOL_outcome) over trailing windows; when conditional entropy drops below a threshold (indicating a regime where alts are tightly coupled to BTC), use the real-time BTC book imbalance sign to trade the alt with the lowest conditional entropy — the key insight is that correlation regimes are non-stationary and detectable from the joint outcome history, so you only trade when the cross-asset coupling is temporarily strong enough to overcome fees.
